question: does replacing the identity with the multiset of all 16-byte windows (no band, minimum 16 bytes) admit short entries and keep L1/L2 and fallback quality on the same 550-entry natural corpus?

fallback_rubric.relevant: the printed sentence answers the query's question or states its point
fallback_rubric.marginal: same document/topic but does not answer the question
fallback_rubric.denominator: all unanchored rows (frozen); the written-group subset is reported separately
fallback_rubric.sample_rule: unanchored rows in report order, every ceil(total/20)-th row, first 20

rules: admission rate for entries < 64 bytes < 0.9 -> window_set_still_gapped

definition.identity: I(r) = multiset { sha256(r[i:i+16])[:16].hex() : 0 <= i <= len(r)-16 }; one token per offset, so repeated windows keep their multiplicity. A record shorter than 16 bytes has an empty identity and is rejected alone. An empty identity is never addressable: it would be covered by every query.
definition.multiplicity_choice: multiset coverage, frozen before the run: count_q(t) >= count_r(t) for every distinct window t. Reason: set inclusion lets one query occurrence pay for a window that occurs twice in the record (repeated table rows/separators); counting is one dict lookup and adds no numeric constant. Multiset coverage implies set inclusion, never the reverse.
definition.protection_band: none, and none is kept. Every identity window lies fully inside the record, so any prefix/suffix leaves every window at offset |p|+i equal to r[i:i+16]. The old PROTECT=6 band belonged to a cut predicate that read bytes before the cut; a fixed window reads only its own bytes.
definition.shortest_addressable_length: MIN_ADDRESSABLE = WINDOW_BYTES = 16 bytes; necessary and sufficient (length alone decides whether the identity is non-empty).
definition.anchor: anchored iff identity(r) is covered by W(q) with multiplicity; 0 anchors -> fallback but still one output; 1 -> matched; >=2 -> ambiguous_multiple_anchors, still top-1 and annotated. Anchors are readings, not exits.
definition.fallback: unanchored reads are ranked by |set(I(r)) & set(W(q))| / |set(I(r))| descending, then address index ascending; fallback_basis = window_overlap when a window is shared, address_order otherwise; no pass/reject threshold.
definition.output_unit: anchored reads print the whole record (unit = record); unanchored reads print the chosen record's sentence with the highest window overlap (unit = sentence, ties by sentence order); spans come from sentences() and always sit on UTF-8 character boundaries at a terminator/newline or the record end.
definition.write: append-only; a record is rejected alone only when its identity is empty (length < 16). Identity containment is not a rejection reason: under a window identity a heading or a table row is legitimately a substring of a longer record, and rejecting containment would filter exactly the short entries this definition exists to admit.
definition.impersonation_cost: If identity(r) is covered by W(q), q must contain every 16-byte window of r as a substring with the record's multiplicity. This does NOT imply q contains r contiguously and does not imply near-verbatim reproduction; the order is lost. Construction: q = r[0:16] + r[1:17] + ... covers every window while never containing r as a contiguous run. Verdict: 'almost verbatim reproduction is required' cannot be derived.
failure_constructions: empty identity kept: covered by every query, anchors every sub-16-byte record; floor one.
set inclusion instead of multiplicity: a repeated window is paid by one query occurrence.
low-entropy windows: a 16-byte run of spaces is shared by any query containing it, so an unrelated query can anchor that record; reported per group, not hidden.
order loss: window coverage is not contiguity (see impersonation_cost).

criteria.C1_closed_state_neutral: the 176-case battery of the frozen output-unit gate replays bit for bit: max|delta| = 0, parameters/state/identity/store signature unchanged, table not allocated, no half-open branch.
criteria.C2_L1: fabricated bytes = 0, illegal spans = 0, UTF-8 decodable = 100%, boundary legal = 100%.
criteria.C3_L2: every output slice hashes to the stored record bytes it claims (faithful).
criteria.C4_L3: per group: usable_and_correct / usable_but_wrong / usable_fallback / unusable.
criteria.C6_fallback: 20 fallback rows sampled mechanically; each printed sentence is scored relevant / marginal / irrelevant against its query; median >= 0.5. The denominator is frozen as **all unanchored rows** (same rule as the previous round); the written-group subset (queries that do have a record in the store) is reported separately as a diagnostic, because unknown/unrelated queries have no answering record by construction.
criteria.V_fabricates: any L1 line fails -> output_fabricates, samples only.
criteria.V_gap: admission rate for entries < 64 bytes < 0.90 -> window_set_still_gapped: write the length limit down, stop adding to the address layer, go to the representation layer.

cost_estimate.estimate_note: closed battery replays the frozen 176-case run (~44 CPU measured last round); the open pass does 2,200 query x 550 record set intersections (~1.2M) plus one sentence scan per fallback. Estimated well below the 200 CPU cap.
